Let \(f\) be the function defined by \(f(x)=e^{x} \cos x\).
(a) Find the average rate of change of \(f\) on the interval \(0 \leq x \leq \pi\).
(b) What is the slope of the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\) ?
(c) Find the absolute minimum value of \(f\) on the interval \(0 \leq x \leq 2 \pi\). Justify your answer.
(d) Let \(g\) be a differentiable function such that \(g\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=0\). The graph of \(g^{\prime}\), the derivative of \(g\), is shown
below. Find the value of \(\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi / 2} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\) or state that it does not exist. Justify your answer.
\includegraphics{ap-calc-ab-2018-frq-05-diagram-01.png}
rawScoringGuide:
\section*{Question 5}
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] The average rate of change of \(f\) on the interval \(0 \leq x \leq \pi\) is \(\frac{f(\pi)-f(0)}{\pi-0}=\frac{-e^{\pi}-1}{\pi}\).
\item[(b)] \(f^{\prime}(x)=e^{x} \cos x-e^{x} \sin x\)
\(f^{\prime}\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)=e^{3 \pi / 2} \cos \left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)-e^{3 \pi / 2} \sin \left(\frac{3 \pi}{2}\right)=e^{3 \pi / 2}\)
The slope of the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\) is \(e^{3 \pi / 2}\).
\item[(c)] \(f^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow \cos x-\sin x=0 \Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{4}, x=\frac{5 \pi}{4}\)

\begin{tabular}[t]{|l|l|}
\hline \(x\) & \(f(x)\) \\
\hline 0 & 1 \\
\hline \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) & \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} e^{\pi / 4}\) \\
\hline \(\frac{5 \pi}{4}\) & \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} e^{5 \pi / 4}\) \\
\hline \(2 \pi\) & \(e^{2 \pi}\) \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
The absolute minimum value of \(f\) on \(0 \leq x \leq 2 \pi\) is \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} e^{5 \pi / 4}\).
\item[(d)] \(\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi / 2} f(x)=0\)
Because \(g\) is differentiable, \(g\) is continuous.
\(\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi / 2} g(x)=g\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=0\)
By L'Hospital's Rule,
\(\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi / 2} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi / 2} \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{g^{\prime}(x)}=\frac{-e^{\pi / 2}}{2}\).
\end{itemize}

1 : answer
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: f^{\prime}(x) \\ 1: \text { slope }\end{array}\right.\)

3 : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { sets } f^{\prime}(x)=0 \\ 1: \text { identifies } x=\frac{\pi}{4}, x=\frac{5 \pi}{4} \\ \text { as candidates } \\ 1: \text { answer with justification }\end{array}\right.\)

3 : \(\left\{\begin{array}{c}1: g \text { is continuous at } x=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \quad \text { and limits equal } 0 \\ 1: \text { applies L'Hospital's Rule } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
